artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation making lake-build-guard.sh's success signal truthful: subcommand validation before dispatch, scope-keyed result sharing, an audible REPLAY marker, the kill -0 wait idiom, a rewritten FAMILY CONVENTIONS block, and 8 new harness cases plus 3 new mutations (27/27 green).

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed lake-build-guard.sh's two false-pass defects (unvalidated lake subcommand passthrough; scope-blind result sharing) and its missing wait-idiom documentation, rewrote the FAMILY CONVENTIONS header block for the dependent sibling guard, and extended the regression suite from 13 to 21 acceptance-mapped cases plus 5 mutations, all passing.

memory_candidates.content: For a bash guard/wrapper script's regression suite, when a defect record asserts a specific exit code for an external tool's error path (e.g. 'lake TARGET exits 0 on unknown command'), verify that assertion against the REAL binary on the target machine before building a test on it. If the real binary's actual behavior differs (version drift, environment difference), build a dedicated deterministic fake reproducing the DOCUMENTED defect shape instead -- never test against the real binary when its live behavior has already been shown to diverge from the recorded defect.

When a result-sharing/caching mechanism keys its replay decision on tree/input staleness alone, that is insufficient if the same unchanged tree can legitimately produce different SCOPES of work (e.g. a scoped build vs. a full build). The fix pattern: hash the invocation's own argument vector (NUL-separated join, never space-joined, to avoid boundary ambiguity) into a scope_key alongside the staleness fingerprint, and treat a missing/empty recorded scope_key as NOT shareable (fail closed) so pre-existing records without the new field never silently over-share.
